findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous due to underscore separator
findings.body: The `userPermDenialCacheKey` function concatenates fields with underscores: `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. Since resource UIDs (name, parent) can themselves contain underscores, different (name, parent) tuples can produce the same key. For example, name="a_b" with parent="" produces the same key as name="a" with parent="b". A denial cached for one resource would incorrectly deny access to a different resource. This can cause false authorization denials for users who should have access.

findings.title: Denial cache key uses raw UserUID which may differ from resolved UID used in permission cache
findings.body: The denial cache key at line 116 uses `checkReq.UserUID` (the raw value parsed from the subject, e.g. a numeric ID like "123"), while the permission cache in `getCachedIdentityPermissions` uses `userIdentifiers.UID` (the resolved UID string like "abc-def"). If the same user is referenced by numeric ID in one request and by UID string in another, the denial cache will not hit for the second request, reducing cache effectiveness. The denial should be cached using the resolved UID to be consistent with the permission cache key.

findings.title: Denial cache test uses unrealistic permission cache value and doesn't prove precedence over an allow
findings.body: The test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` in the permission cache. In production, `getScopeMap` only ever stores `true` values, so a `false` value is never present. The comment says 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked' but a `false` value would not grant access anyway (`checkPermission` checks `scopeMap[...]` which evaluates to false). To properly test that the denial cache takes precedence over a granting permission cache entry, the test should set `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}` and verify the response is still denied.
